reviewNotes: HOLD. This is the AIS domestic/local-number prepaid path, distinct from canonical SIM2Fly. AIS currently supports prepaid eSIM conversion/transfer with passport verification and current prepaid add-ons can add validity days; 2026 community users report stable SMS reception and roughly THB10/month retention. The reviewed provider evidence does not support the stronger community claim that a small top-up extends three years, and a universal foreign-user remote-acquisition/China OTP path is not established.

events.outcome: AIS local prepaid supports eSIM/passport identity handling and provider prepaid offers can add service-validity days. 2026 community users report low monthly keep costs and fast SMS reception, but stronger multi-year low-cost extension claims remain unverified against current provider rules.

data.acquisitionSummary: AIS domestic prepaid is a separate route from SIM2Fly. AIS supports eSIM conversion/transfer with ID-card or passport verification; current foreign-user remote-new-number acquisition details are not fully reconciled in this bounded review.

keep.action: Current AIS prepaid add-on material includes a THB30 prepaid call package that grants an additional 30 days of service validity. Community users report lower effective keep costs around THB10/month, but a universal cheapest keep mechanism and multi-year extension rule are not provider-reconciled here.

data.chinaActivation: Current provider evidence supports passport-based eSIM handling but does not establish a guaranteed mainland-China-first acquisition/activation path for a new AIS domestic number.
data.kyc: AIS eSIM conversion/transfer flows accept passport-number verification for applicable subscribers. New-number foreign-customer registration/acquisition requirements remain scope-limited here.
data.payment: Current prepaid top-up/package purchase mechanisms exist; remote foreign payment reliability is not established.
data.roamingSms: A 2026 community user reports AIS signal and fast SMS reception in the keep-number context, but location and third-party OTP coverage are not sufficiently controlled to make a mainland-China guarantee.
data.holdReason: Distinct AIS local-number route is real, but the cheapest durable keep mechanic, foreign remote acquisition and mainland-China OTP behavior are not sufficiently reconciled; reject the unverified multi-year extension claim.
data.tariffSummary: Provider evidence supports prepaid validity increments and passport-based eSIM handling; HOLD pending a settled low-cost annual keep mechanic and foreign/China operational proof.
guideSteps: Treat this as AIS domestic prepaid, not SIM2Fly.
Verify foreign new-number registration/acquisition eligibility before purchase.
Use only provider-confirmed validity increments; do not rely on unverified multi-year top-up claims.
